description: TEMPLATE. Copy to databricks_manifest.json (git-ignored) and fill in with your own workspace's values, or let the generate-artifact-manifest skill write it after a deploy. The real manifest records every Databricks resource the OmniView deployment created; deploy/databricks/tear_down.py deletes exactly those, in order, and nothing else.
_usage: then replace every <PLACEHOLDER> below with the values for your workspace.
The real file is git-ignored on purpose: it is deployment state, not source, and
it names a live Postgres endpoint and service principal. Operational knowledge
that is NOT deployment-specific lives in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, not here.

info.app_resources: see deploy/databricks/app_create.json (postgres branch/database + secret scope binding)
info.user_api_scopes: sql (applied via deploy/databricks/app_update.json; iam.* read scopes are implicit defaults; jobs scopes are rejected by the Free Edition validator - the Admin Portal's Jobs tab falls back to the app identity)
info.sql_warehouse_id: <warehouse id the Admin Portal reads system.billing through - pre-existing, NOT created by this deployment, never torn down>
info._redeploy_log: The real manifest also accumulates one 'redeploy_<date>' note per rebuild: what shipped, which service principal replaced which, whether datavault had to be rebuilt. Useful history, but deployment-specific - keep it in the ignored file.
info._operational_notes: The hazards that used to be documented in this block (Lakebase soft-delete + slug reservation, `apps update` replacing the whole app spec, schema-ownership and the object-ownership self-healing mechanisms) are NOT deployment-specific and now live in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. Read that before any teardown or redeploy.

resources.notes: The Databricks App (compute + its auto-created service principal + the resource bindings to the Lakebase branch and secret scope). Deleting it removes all of those.

Synced app source bundle (mirror of dist/databricks_app). Carries one ACL: CAN_READ for the app service principal (dies with the folder). Safe to delete; rebuilt by deploy/databricks/build_app.py + databricks workspace import-dir.
Holds one secret: secret-key (Django SECRET_KEY). Deleting the scope deletes the key.

DESTROYS ALL APP DATA: the production branch holds the omniview schema (auth/sessions + uploaded CSVs + budget map) and the datavault schema (warehouse). A local Data/Banks tree remains as the re-import source.
